command: Build/install the core, Prefect, SQL, SQLModel, FastAPI, and test-backend wheels in a fresh Python 3.11 environment. With PYTHONPATH unset: python -m pytest -o pythonpath= -q tests/prefect -m prefect.
result: The installed-wheel live Prefect/PostgreSQL suite passed: 41 passed in 49.72s with no skips. Installed-wheel headless/FastAPI route parity passed: 1 passed in 0.53s.
assertions: The isolated installed test backend stages a target write, then commits one row independently of the connector transaction and pauses at a marker before the Process worker is killed.
At the fault boundary the canonical execution effect has no receipt, the sink contains exactly the independently committed row, and the connector effect ledger has no record.

After releasing and hard-killing the Process worker, recovery records both abandoned attempts as lost and the canonical effect as unknown; the submission remains failed and the effectful write is not replayed.

A final PostgreSQL read confirms the partial row remains exactly once and the effect ledger remains empty. This tests host recovery behavior under a non-transactional partial effect; it does not qualify an external connector implementation.

runtime.prefect_server: Separately supervised API process backed by per-test PostgreSQL databases
runtime.worker_backend_plugin: Separately built and installed etlantic-phase058-test-worker-plugin 0.1.0 wheel

source_sha256_method: SHA-256 over sorted repository-relative source paths and file bytes, with NUL separators.
limitations: The injected independent PostgreSQL commit models a connector that has applied an external partial effect before acknowledging the batch. It does not prove that a production or third-party connector exposes equivalent semantics or reports reconciliation data.
This local campaign exercises CPython 3.11.15, Prefect 3.7.8, PostgreSQL 16.13, and Process workers only; the remote CI run and full version/hosting matrix remain open.

ci_configuration.database_service: Local PostgreSQL 16.13; per-test SQLModel rows and Prefect databases were cleaned.
ci_configuration.server_process: Separate Prefect API process with PostgreSQL persistence

cleanup: The test uses unique tenant, workspace, submission, deployment, sink-table, effect-ledger, and database identities; scoped rows are removed by the fixture.
The per-test Prefect server stopped and its dedicated database was dropped; the shared local PostgreSQL service and temporary installed-wheel environment remain available.
